output.summary: Succulent plant of unclear native origin, now ranging from North Africa and southern Europe through Asia to Australasia; much of this spread is assumed to be human-assisted, and its status in the Americas is uncertain. It has reddish, mostly ground-hugging stems and small yellow flowers that open briefly on sunny mornings. All parts are edible raw or cooked, and the seeds can be eaten or made into flour, though the leaves contain high oxalate levels.
